Security Tracking Issue

Do not make this issue public.

NOTE THIS ISSUE IS CURRENTLY EMBARGOED, DO NOT MAKE PUBLIC COMMITS OR COMMENTS ABOUT THIS ISSUE.

WARNING: NOTICE THAT CHANGING THE SECURITY LEVEL FROM "SECURITY ISSUE" TO "RED HAT INTERNAL" MAY BREAK THE EMBARGO.

Flaw:
-----

mTLS passthrough
https://bugzilla.redhat.com/show_bug.cgi?id=2319217

Deployments of Keycloak with a reverse proxy not using pass-through
termination of TLS, with mTLS enabled, are affected by an issue where an
attacker on the local network can authenticate as any user or client that
leverages mTLS as the authentication mechanism.

Trusted proxies introduced in Keycloak 26 can mitigate this to some extent
by only accepting certificates from proxy headers if the request is coming
from the IP address of the proxy. However, this is a very weak form of authentication as IP addresses can in many cases be spoofed.

The attacker would need to have access to the local network, and in
addition gain access to the corresponding public certificates, which in
many cases is not the hardest thing to do, especially considering that we
are assuming an insider, or an attacker that has gained access to the local
network.

Additionally, Keycloak can further be configured to not only obtain
certificates through HTTP headers, but also to not validate the
certificates. If this option is enabled for a deployment the attacker does
not have to obtain the actual public certificate, and can simply generate a
random one with for example openssl with whatever subject they want.

~~~

Keycloak TLS passthrough
https://bugzilla.redhat.com/show_bug.cgi?id=2319217

Deployments of Keycloak with a reverse proxy not using pass-through
termination of TLS, with mTLS enabled, are affected by an issue where an
attacker on the local network can authenticate as any user or client that
leverages mTLS as the authentication mechanism.

Trusted proxies introduced in Keycloak 26 can mitigate this to some extent
by only accepting certificates from proxy headers if the request is coming
from the IP address of the proxy. However, this is a very weak form of authentication as IP addresses can in many cases be spoofed.

The attacker would need to have access to the local network, and in
addition gain access to the corresponding public certificates, which in
many cases is not the hardest thing to do, especially considering that we
are assuming an insider, or an attacker that has gained access to the local
network.

Additionally, Keycloak can further be configured to not only obtain
certificates through HTTP headers, but also to not validate the
certificates. If this option is enabled for a deployment the attacker does
not have to obtain the actual public certificate, and can simply generate a
random one with for example openssl with whatever subject they want.

items.fromString:
Just a heads-up that the RHBK 24 server may not work OOTB with the RH-SSO 7.6 OIDC client adapters.

h2. Mitigation

There is the mitigation that people will need to enable the switch "Exclude Issuer From Authentication Response" in the admin console, which should be done for every RHBK client pointed to application secured by RH-SSO 7.6 adapters. It can be done in the admin console when going to the particular client -> tab "Advanced" -> section "OpenID Connect Compatibility Modes" . 

h2.  Details

This is the side-effect of adding the `iss` parameter to OIDC authentication response, which is supported by the OAuth 2.1 specification [2] to avoid mix-up attacks [3]. This is documented in the documentation of Keycloak 23 [4] and it would be documented also in RHBK 24 migration documentation, but it is not explicitly documented that this affects all the RH-SSO 7.6 clients.

h2. Bug description

Customers will detect if they have such issue that they would not be able to login to their application due the code-to-token request sent by the adapter would fail. They will see errors in their RH-SSO 7.6 log like:
```
[OAuthRequestAuthenticator] failed to turn code into token
[OAuthRequestAuthenticator] status from server: 403
```
due the incorrect redirect_uri and in the server.log they would see CODE_TO_TOKEN_ERROR event.

h2. Possible fix

Adding one line of including `iss` parameter here should fix this https://gitlab.cee.redhat.com/keycloak/keycloak-prod/-/blob/18.0.x/adapters/oidc/adapter-core/src/main/java/org/keycloak/adapters/OAuthRequestAuthenticator.java?ref_type=heads#L387 (It is already done in latest Keycloak main https://github.com/keycloak/keycloak/blob/24.0.3/adapters/oidc/adapter-core/src/main/java/org/keycloak/adapters/OAuthRequestAuthenticator.java#L388 ).

[2] https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/html/draft-ietf-oauth-v2-1-10#name-authorization-response
[3] https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/html/draft-ietf-oauth-security-topics-24#section-4.4
[4] https://www.keycloak.org/docs/latest/upgrading/index.html#added-iss-parameter-to-oauth-2-0openid-connect-authentication-response

items.toString: Memory Leak within RH-SSO infinispan caches (standalone mode)

items.fromString:
*1. Issue description*


RH-SSO standalone mode does also contains embedded caches.
here is the 7.6.6 standalone.xml

~~~
    <local-cache name="sessions"/>
    <local-cache name="authenticationSessions"/>
    <local-cache name="offlineSessions"/>
    <local-cache name="clientSessions"/>
    <local-cache name="offlineClientSessions"/>
    <local-cache name="loginFailures"/>
~~~

There is a memory leak issue with local embedded caches


*2. Similar existing (fixed in SSO 7.6.1 for stranalone-HA mode)*

There was in issue with distributed caches which has been fixed since:
-KEYCLOAK-18518 - (fixed in KC 15) - Expired cache objects in infinispan cache are never garbage collected and lead to out of memory [1]

-RHSSO-2169 - fixed in RH-SSO 7.6.1 - Expired cache objects in infinispan cache are never garbage collected in standalone configuration [2].


For further information, see also KCS article:

-SSO 7.6 OOME due to org.infinispan.container.impl.DefaultSegmentedDataContainer [3]



*3. Existing Work-around*
The issue  faced (standalone mode) is similar to RH-SSO-2169, which has been fixed in RH-SSO 7.6.1  for standalone-ha mode,  but not for the standalone mode.


In standalone mode, you should apply the same work-around/solution that is indicated within the KCS to circumvent this issue:

You need to add expiration and eviction for cache container keycloak. Add expiration in all locals cache as it is shown below.


here is the 7.6.6 standalone.xml

~~~
    <local-cache name="sessions"/>
    <local-cache name="authenticationSessions"/>
    <local-cache name="offlineSessions"/>
    <local-cache name="clientSessions"/>
    <local-cache name="offlineClientSessions"/>
    <local-cache name="loginFailures"/>
~~~

It needs to be updated as follows using jboss cli:

~~~
/subsystem=infinispan/cache-container=keycloak/local-cache=sessions/component=expiration/:write-attribute(name=lifespan,value=2000000000)
/subsystem=infinispan/cache-container=keycloak/local-cache=clientSessions/component=expiration/:write-attribute(name=lifespan,value=2000000000)
/subsystem=infinispan/cache-container=keycloak/local-cache=offlineSessions/component=expiration/:write-attribute(name=lifespan,value=2000000000)
/subsystem=infinispan/cache-container=keycloak/local-cache=offlineClientSessions/component=expiration/:write-attribute(name=lifespan,value=2000000000)
/subsystem=infinispan/cache-container=keycloak/local-cache=authenticationSessions/component=expiration/:write-attribute(name=lifespan,value=2000000000)
/subsystem=infinispan/cache-container=keycloak/local-cache=loginFailures/component=expiration/:write-attribute(name=lifespan,value=2000000000)
/subsystem=infinispan/cache-container=keycloak/local-cache=actionTokens/component=expiration/:write-attribute(name=lifespan,value=2000000000)
~~~
 

 

 

 

 

 

[1] https://issues.redhat.com/browse/KEYCLOAK-18518

[2] https://issues.redhat.com/browse/RHSSO-2169

[3] https://access.redhat.com/solutions/7011043

<spi name="user">

- add the property: **/spi=mySPI/:map-put(name=properties, key=storageProviderTimeout, value=10000)

From SSOSUP-636:

RH-SSO for OpenShift cluster results in a "split brain" state after RH-SSO database outage.

The cluster MERGE process eventually starts, but "split brain" state lasts a few minutes.

Steps to reproduce
1. Deploy RH-SSO for OpenShift + PostgreSQL(Persistent) instance with 2 replicas by Template or RH-SSO Operator
2. Wait until RH-SSO instance fully up, and then stop PostgreSQL pod by making its replicas=0
3. Check the RH-SSO container in these pods start restarting repeatdly.
4. Start PostgreSQL pod. It will remove roadblocks of RH-SSO containers boot process.
5. All RH-SSO containers try to find other nodes in the cluster with  jgroups "dns.DNS_PING" module simultaneously, but they fails because they are all not in OpenShift "Ready" state, and "dns.DNS_PING" module cannot detect non "Ready" nodes.
6. RH-SSO containers all emits log like this, and result in "Split Brain" state.
```
　INFO  [org.jgroups.protocols.pbcast.GMS] (ServerService Thread Pool – 76) keycloak-0: no members discovered after 3008 ms: creating cluster as coordinator
```
7. After a few minutes, they will detect each other and start MERGE process, but it happens only after start receiving user traffic because 'READY' state is the trigger of MERGE and traffic routing.

Note: 
This happen for instances deployed by RH-SSO Operator too. Instances deployed by RH-SSO Operator uses "StatefulSet", which guarantees orderd pod sheduling, but it doesn't prevent simultaneous container restart in the already deployed Pods. 

Is there any way to avoid split brain state?

OCP/RH-SSO operator 7.6.4

*2) Usual Operator image deployment*

RH-SSO operators pulls 2 images from the registry
-sso image 
-PostgreSQL image

*3) Using an Airgap environment (i.e disconnected environment)*

When working in a disconnected environment and using Openshift 4.12 ICSP (ImageContentSourcePolicy) mirroring, images are pulled from mirrors.  But ImageContentSourcePolicy objects support image digests only, not image tags.

See Openshift Doc 4.12

Configuring image registry repository mirroring
https://docs.openshift.com/container-platform/4.12/openshift_images/image-configuration.html#images-configuration-registry-mirror_image-configuration

_~~~
5.  To check that the mirrored configuration settings, 

e. Pull an image digest to the node from the source and check if it is resolved by the mirror. ImageContentSourcePolicy objects support image digests only, not image tags.
~~~
_
 ===> The Openshift doc clearly states that it requires to pull image using image digest.


*4. Issue Description:*

When working in disconnected environment (Airgap) and using Openshift ICSP, all the objects have to be pulled using image digest.

In the case of OCP/RH-SSO operator 7.6.4 deployed on Openshift 4.12, the PostgreSQL image is pulled is retrieved  using image tag.

In the usual way, when user can have access to Red Hat source registry, OCP/RH-SSO operator image deployment is working  absolutely fine.

In the case of working within a Air Gap environment, and using  Openshift ICSP, OCP/RH-SSO operator image deployment is is FAILING, as it cannot pull the PostgreSQL image from the mirror within the airgap environment.

It generates an error 

_" Failed to pull image "registry.access.redhat.com/rhscl/postgresql-10-rhel7:173": rpc error: code = Unknown desc = parsing image configuration: Error fetching blob: invalid status code from registry 403 (Forbidden)" _


*5 What is needed to make it work*

In order to deploy OCP/RH-SSO operator images safely within an disconnected/airgap environment the PostgreSQL image has to be pulled using image digest and not image tag.

Note:
The sso image is already pulled using image digest, and is obtained correctly

apply CR on cluster

reapply with changes

apply changes in Admin Console

Red Hat must scan offerings for known malware, ensuring the artifacts shipped to our customers are malware free. If malware is found, the release build should be aborted, and the findings should be investigated and remediated before the artifacts ship to our customers.

RH-SSO is on the list of products that needs to meet the attestation requirements by the end of 2023. [Malware scanning is one of those requirements|https://docs.google.com/document/d/1QMrM5ac2sbecmy7lYHA8S6p8L8ivVwHlgdcspy-Z4VE/edit?usp=sharing]. From the experience with other teams, it should be possible to achieve it by introducing [3 lines of code into CPaaS pipeline](https://gitlab.cee.redhat.com/cpaas-products/openshift-jenkins/-/blob/master/versions/ocp-tools-4.14-rhel-8/release.yml#L37-L39).

h2. Place in the offering lifecycle

After the binaries are built in the release pipeline, the malware scan should be performed automatically, using updated malware signatures. After the scan is successful and no malware is found, the build is tagged as successful for further processing and release. Any positive detection should abort the build, investigate the findings and remediate before tagging the build as successful and ready to ship.

h2. Roles and Responsibilities

No actions are required when the malware signatures are current, and no malware is found.
The Offering team will investigate and remediate if malware is found during the scan.
If the workflow fails to verify whether the malware signatures are current, the Pipeline maintainer (TBD) will be responsible for ensuring the signatures are updated.


Implement malware scanning into the pipeline (the easiest mechanism would likely be through cpaas).

See: [https://gitlab.cee.redhat.com/cpaas-products/openshift-jenkins/-/blob/master/versions/ocp-tools-4.14-rhel-8/release.yml#L37-L39]

items.fromString:
*Summary:* SSO clusters (done via jgroups) between two OCP versions OCP 3 and OCP 4.

*Background:*

We are running a RHSSO cluster in OCP platforms (OCP 3.11 and OCP 4.10). We are on the OCP3 to OCP4 migration period. There is a network maintenance on Jun 25, 2023 (around 2am). After the network maintenance, there is cluster communication issue between RHSSO nodes. Attempt to kill and replace the leader pod don't work and we finally need to restart all the RHSSO nodes (and gossip router nodes) so as to resume the service. We want to have investigate the root cause of why the RHSSO cluster not able to resume after network maintenance and to make configuration change, if needed, so as to avoid cluster auto-resume issue.

*Specs:*

Rhsso 7.6.2 makes use of  jgroups 4.2.15, which has a bug due to which  one or more gossip router never get reconnected.

The fix was implemented on Jgroups 5.x and from Jira JGRP-2713 was backported, see below:

*Jira(s) details:*
||Jira||Purpose||Conclusion||
|JGRP-2713|Discuss the issue|The fix has been backported in jgroups version 4.2.23 and testing jar is provided  by Bela Ban|
|EAPSUP-1237|Verify with EAP if a cluster with members in OCP 3 and OCP 4 is supported|team gave the ok |

*Request*

Since Rhsso is bundled with Jgroups we need to test the jgroups jar so that this patch can be released to the customer.
